newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan may see forex gain due to weak yen -- MITI.
newsitem.headline: Japan may see forex gain due to weak yen -- MITI.

text.p: Japan may see a slight net foreign exchange gain in the 1997 industrial trade balance due to a weaker yen, but the impact on the economy as a whole will be limited, the Ministry of International Trade and Industry (MITI) said on Monday.

Based on preliminary calculations using an exchange rate of around 118 yen to the dollar, the average rate in January, and assuming the exchange rate continues at this level for all of 1997, Japan would see a slight forex gain of around 650 billion yen in the industrial trade balance, a MITI official said.
The average yen rate for January was down by a little over 11 percent compared with January 1996, when it averaged around 105 yen to the dollar.

According to the calculations, which assume a dollar rate of around 105 yen for all of 1996, export payments would rise by around 3.25 trillion yen over the course of 1997, while import payments would fall to around 2.60 trillion yen for an overall gain of 650 billion yen, the official said.
While this state might cause problems for certain sectors, especially petroleum, the overall economic impact would be small, even if it continues for some time, he added.

"In comparison with nominal gross domestic product (GDP) figures, an increase of this magnitude is basically in equilibrium, meaning its overall impact in a macroeconomic sense will be limited," he said.
The figures were reached using data concerning 47 different private industries, including domestic agriculture, real estate, and the automotive industry.
